runtimes.name: Node.js
runtimes.notes: Covered by the `compat` CI job on every version and by the full Vitest suite. 20.x is upstream EOL (2026-04-30) and is retained for the 2.x line; 22.x is in maintenance and 24.x is the active LTS.

runtimes.name: Bun
runtimes.notes: Covered by the `compat` CI job. The ESM entry points, the Vitest suite (`bun test`) and the build all run unmodified.

runtimes.name: Browsers (evergreen)
runtimes.notes: Baseline is ES2022 plus `fetch`, `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder` and `crypto.getRandomValues`; `./vault` additionally needs `crypto.subtle`. Optional peers are the app bundler's responsibility.

runtimes.name: React Native
runtimes.notes: Needs a `crypto.getRandomValues` polyfill (`react-native-get-random-values`) loaded before the SDK, plus `Buffer` if the app imports `@stellar/stellar-sdk` directly. `installReactNativePolyfills()` covers `atob`, `btoa`, `TextEncoder` and `TextDecoder`.

runtimes.name: Deno
runtimes.notes: Use npm specifiers. Verified by static review only — the compat job does not provision a Deno runtime yet.

runtimes.name: Cloudflare Workers / Vercel Edge
runtimes.notes: The browser bundle check covers the same module graph. Optional peers must be bundled explicitly when the edge entry point you use needs them.

peers.name: @stellar/stellar-sdk
peers.notes: Required by `./chains/stellar`: the transaction builders, event filters and announcement parsing are re-exported from that entry point. Marked optional so apps that only use the EVM, CKB, Solana or vault entry points are not forced to install it.

peers.name: @solana/web3.js
peers.notes: Only `fetchAnnouncements()` needs it, and it imports the package dynamically on demand. Address derivation and scanning use the in-tree base58 encoder, so importing `./chains/solana` — or the package root — works without this peer installed.

peers.name: viem
peers.notes: A regular dependency, not a peer: the EVM and CKB modules use its hex and keccak helpers, and the wallet event normalizer uses `getAddress`. Bundled with the package, so consumers never install it separately.
